claim: For f(n) the number of solutions (x,y,z) to 4/n = 1/x+1/y+1/z, the summatory function over primes satisfies N log^2 N << sum_{p<=N} f(p) << N log^2 N log log N as N -> infinity.
stance_target: asymptotic counting of three-term unit-fraction equation solutions
scope_conditions: numerator fixed at 4 (Erdos-Straus equation), n=p ranges over primes p<=N
quoted_support: Our main result establishes the asymptotic upper and lower bounds N log^2 N << sum_{p leq N} f(p) << N log^2 N log log N.
numbers: N log^2 N log log N

claim: The pointwise bound f(p) << p^{3/5} + O(1/log log p) holds for all primes p, and f(p) = O(log^3 p log log p) for a density-1 subset of primes.
stance_target: typical multiplicity of a single three-term unit-fraction representation
quoted_support: we have f(p) = O(log^3 p log log p) for a subset of primes of density arbitrarily close to 1; thus a typical prime has a relatively small number of solutions to the Erdos-Straus Diophantine equation. We also... establish the bound f(p) << p^{3/5} + O(1/log log p) for all primes p.

claim: This paper's counting apparatus addresses the multiplicity of a single fixed-numerator three-term unit-fraction equation (4/n), not pairs of triples matched on two independent symmetric functions (equal sum AND equal reciprocal sum), so it is a technique-adjacent but not directly-applicable precedent for Section 5's problem.
stance_target: prior art for Section 5's two-triple equal-sum-and-equal-reciprocal-sum Diophantine problem
scope_conditions: three-term unit fraction equation, single triple per equation
quoted_support: For any positive integer n, let f(n) denote the number of solutions to the Diophantine equation 4/n = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z with x,y,z positive integers.
